ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French AML/CFT framework: Loi n° 2013-1117 du 6 décembre 2013 relative à la lutte contre la fraude fiscale et la grande délinquance économique et financière; Loi n° 2016-1691 du 9 décembre 2016 (Loi Sapin II); Loi n° 2018-898 du 23 octobre 2018 (Loi relative à la lutte contre la fraude); Loi n° 2020-1674 du 24 décembre 2020 (Loi PACTE, amended by Ordonnance n° 2020-115 du 12 février 2020); Articles 561-1 to 561-50 of the Code monétaire et financier (CMF); Article L. 123-1 Code de commerce (RCS filings); Décret n° 2017-1094 du 12 juin 2017 (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Arrêté du 26 juin 2017 relatif au registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Directive (EU) 2015/849 (AMLD IV), Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD V), Directive (EU) 2024/1640 (AMLD VI) for transposition; TRACFIN (Traitement du renseignement et action contre les circuits financiers clandestins) is the financial intelligence unit. ACPR (Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution) and AMF (Autorité des marchés financiers) are supervisory authorities. The Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) is maintained by the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against: (1) French PEP lists maintained by ACPR/AMF and TRACFIN; (2) EU Consolidated Sanctions List; (3) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (4) OFAC SDN List and OFAC Sectoral Sanctions Identifications (SSI) List; (5) UK HMT/OFSI Sanctions List; (6) Interpol and Europol wanted persons databases; (7) French domestic list of persons subject to asset freezes (Registre national des gels) maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required for all foreign PEPs and for UBOs resident in high-risk third countries identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF). Screening must be conducted at onboarding and periodically (at minimum annually) and upon any trigger event (change of UBO, significant transaction, adverse media). The shipbuilding sector, per ACPR guidance and CMF Article L. 561-10, is classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced due to dual-use export control and maritime security concerns; simplified due diligence is not permitted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr) for RCS filings; INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) for trademark conflict search; Guichet Unique (procedures.inpi.fr) for business formalities since 2023; and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) held by the Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court) of the competent jurisdiction.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to Article L. 123-1 of the Code de commerce and the Loi Toubon (Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994 relative à l'emploi de la langue française), the company name (dénomination sociale) may be in French or a foreign language, but all registration documents, articles of association, and public filings must be in French. If the name is in a foreign language, a French transliteration is required for the RCS. The name must not be generic, deceptive, or infringe prior trademarks. For a SAS, the name must be followed by 'SAS' or 'Société par Actions Simplifiée'. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name in the same or related commercial sector; the INPI conducts a similarity search. For container vessel shipbuilding, the name may include industry-specific terms such as 'Chantiers Navals', 'Construction Navale', or 'Maritime', but such terms do not confer any exclusive right.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name reservation by the INPI or the RCS, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the INPI within 30 days of notification, or a contentious appeal (recours contentieux) before the Tribunal Judiciaire of Paris within 2 months. The appeal must include: (1) proof of the original filing; (2) the rejection decision; (3) arguments demonstrating that the name is not confusingly similar to prior trademarks or registered names; (4) evidence of consent from prior trademark holders if applicable; (5) a new name reservation request with alternative names. For SAS incorporation, the name reservation certificate (certificat de réservation de dénomination) is valid for 30 days and may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon written request to the INPI. If the name includes a prohibited or sensitive token, prior ministerial approval (autorisation ministérielle) must be obtained before the RCS will accept the filing; the appeal must be directed to the relevant ministry (e.g., Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances for financial tokens, Ministère des Armées for defense tokens).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permitted for a SAS engaged in commercial shipbuilding of deep-sea dry cargo and container vessels (ISIC 3011). Pursuant to Article L. 123-11-1 of the Code de commerce and Article 2 of Décret n° 2017-1094, the registered office must be a physical address where the company can be reached for service of process and where its effective management is located. For shipbuilding activities requiring statutory licenses (Autorisation d'Exercice de la Profession de Constructeur Naval), the registered office must be a verifiable industrial site with adequate infrastructure (dry docks, slipways, fabrication halls). The use of a virtual office or domiciliation service is incompatible with the industrial licensing requirements of the Direction Générale de l'Armement (DGA) and the Ministry of the Sea for shipbuilding, and may trigger administrative penalties, including rejection of the RCS filing and fines under Article L. 123-11-2 of the Code de commerce.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (75-90%). The DGA, the Direction Générale de la Mer, and the Ministry of the Economy conduct unannounced physical inspections of shipbuilding sites to verify compliance with industrial licensing, export control regulations, and environmental standards. Additionally, tax authorities (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques) may conduct on-site inspections to verify the reality of the commercial substance and the transfer pricing documentation. The ACPR and TRACFIN may also conduct inspections if the company is subject to enhanced AML/CFT obligations. The likelihood is quantified at 75-90% within the first 12 months of operation, given the strategic nature of the shipbuilding sector and the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Title II, Chapter VII, Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-4 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); Articles L. 210-1 to L. 210-10 (formation and capacity); Articles R. 123-101 et seq. and R. 123-160 (registration and RCS formalities).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) kept by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, with electronic filing via the INPI-operated Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Demande d'immatriculation au RCS (formulaire M0/M des sociétés) transmitted through the Guichet unique, accompanied by the executed statuts, attestation de dépôt de fonds, déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif, and attestation de parution dans un support d'annonces légales.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for an SAS; the articles of association freely fix the capital. Cash contributions must be fully paid into a blocked account held by a French credit institution or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and funds may only be released after RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory appraiser's report (commissaire aux apports) unless legal relief applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-forma First Board Resolution — [Company], SAS. The shareholders, acting on the recorded date, unanimously resolve: (1) share capital of €[Y] is subscribed and divided into [X] shares; each cash subscription shall remain deposited in a blocked escrow account until RCS registration; (2) registered office is fixed at [Address], in the jurisdiction of the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; (3) [Name] is appointed Président, with full powers of day-to-day management and representation, and [Name] is appointed Directeur Général, with concurrent powers; (4) the President is authorized to complete all formalities, including publication of legal notices and RCS filing. (Certified extract.)

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Association and Appointment of First Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel and shareholders, followed by verification through the INPI/Infogreffe RCS database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft final French-language statuts for the SAS, verify the proposed corporate name against the RCS database, set share capital and classes of shares, define governance roles of the Président and Directeur Général, and obtain the signed acceptance of the first officers. If in-kind contributions are made, appoint a commissaire aux apports to prepare the valuation report before execution.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all shareholders and officers
Draft and final statuts signed by shareholders
Valuation report of commissaire aux apports, if applicable
Bank certificate of capital deposit or blocked escrow certificate
Proof of registered office address (lease, sublease or accommodation certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the corporate name is refused due to conflict, submit alternative names and amend the statuts; if in-kind valuation is challenged, obtain a supplementary appraiser report or substitute cash consideration before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-Up Capital in a Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation, deposit the full amount of cash subscriptions, and obtain a certificate from the depositary (attestation de blocage des fonds) confirming that funds are unavailable until the company is registered with the RCS. Where the registered office is held in a branch of the same bank, ensure the depositary is independent of the subscriber.
required_dossiers: Copy of the draft statuts
Identification of the legal representative or person empowered to receive funds
Cash subscription payment order or bank transfer record
Attestation de dépôt des fonds signed by the depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the escrow due to AML/KYC queries, complete enhanced due diligence, identify all signatories, and resupply source-of-funds documentation; if the funds are under the statutory minimum selected in the articles, increase the deposit accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Incorporation File to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI for the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into the Guichet unique, select 'création d'une société par actions simplifiée', complete the M0/M1 electronic forms, upload the statuts, proof of deposit, proof of address, beneficial ownership declaration and identity documents, then pay the applicable state and greffe fees online. The platform verifies dossier completeness and routes the file to the competent greffe.
required_dossiers: Electronic M0/M1 forms
Signed statuts (certified if notarized)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs
Justificatif de domiciliation / lease agreement
Identity and proof of address of each shareholder and officer
Receipt of online fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet unique issues a non-complete dossier notice, submit the specified supplementary documents within the statutory period; if the filing is blocked by a conflict or prior judicial opposition, cure the defect or provide a court clearance order before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Issuance of Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) via Infogreffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After validation by the Guichet unique, the competent greffe examines the legal regularity of the statuts and the registration file. Upon approval, the company is assigned a SIREN/SIRET number and an extract Kbis is issued as the official proof of legal existence and authority of the officers.
required_dossiers: Complete electronic file transferred from the Guichet unique
Attestation de parution in an authorized legal announcements newspaper
Confirmation of payment of greffe fees
Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs with supporting identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe suspends registration due to defective statuts or missing legal announcement, correct the document and refile via the Guichet unique; if the Kbis is delayed beyond the SLA, request a certificate of filing (certificat de dépôt) from the greffe and, if necessary, petition the court for judicial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Publication and Post-Registration Administrative Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales authorized in the department of the registered office; Guichet unique for social and tax notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the incorporation notice in an approved legal gazette within the required deadline, obtain the attestation de parution, then complete the post-registration declarations through the Guichet unique for social security (URSSAF), tax registration, and business license notifications. Retain all certificates in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Attestation de parution of the legal notice
RCS Kbis extract
SIRET/EDIFACT notification
URSSAF employer registration forms
Application forms for any sector-specific license required for marine vessel construction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the legal notice is defective, publish a corrective notice and file the correction with the greffe; if registration with URSSAF is delayed, forward the attestation of prior electronic filing and RCS Kbis to obtain expedited social security registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) under the Préfet de département, together with the Direction interrégionale de la mer (DIRM) where the shipyard occupies coastal or port public domain.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation environnementale au titre des installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE) for the operation of the commercial shipyard and, where relevant, an occupation permit (titre d'occupation) for port or maritime public domain.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) - Inspection des installations classées
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full Environmental Impact Assessment (étude d'impact) with public inquiry under Articles L. 181-1 et seq. and R. 181-1 et seq. of the French Environmental Code, as the construction of ocean-going container vessels at an industrial shipyard falls within the 'Autorisation' category of ICPE and requires a detailed risk assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the IED Directive (2010/75/EU), French ICPE arrêtés for shipbuilding, Water Framework Directive thresholds for wastewater and stormwater discharge, solvent VOC emission ceilings under Decree No. 2018-800, hazardous waste declaration and tracking under GEREP, and emergency response standards for storage of flammable and toxic substances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the local fire safety commission after inspection, structural load inspection and clearance for slipways, quays, dry docks, gantry cranes and hull assembly halls by an approved technical control bureau, and workplace health and safety authorization from the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du travail), including compliance with electrical, machinery, confined-space and vessel-in-build access rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Non-established foreign businesses generally deal with the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). The principal online portals are impots.gouv.fr and the professional account (espace professionnel); business-formation formalities are filed through the Guichet unique operated by INPI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the Guichet unique. Upon registration, it receives a SIREN and establishment-specific SIRET from INSEE; the SIREN is its principal French business identifier. It must obtain or confirm its French VAT number (FR followed by a two-character key and the nine-digit SIREN) with the competent SIE before making transactions requiring VAT registration. A foreign company without a French establishment applies to the SIEE for VAT identification before commencing taxable French transactions; the application normally includes proof of legal existence, constitutional documents, evidence of business activity, identity and authority of representatives, and transaction details. A business established in another EU Member State generally does not appoint a French fiscal representative. A business established outside the EU generally must appoint a French fiscal representative, subject to applicable legal exceptions or mutual-assistance arrangements. Foreign taxable persons making domestic taxable supplies generally have no small-business registration threshold and must register when required by the nature of their transactions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) by default. Certain qualifying young companies may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, IR), generally for up to five fiscal years, if statutory conditions are met, including age, ownership, workforce, turnover or balance-sheet, and non-listing requirements. The election is not an unrestricted check-the-box election and does not make a SAS generally pass-through eligible. No general French check-the-box or elective hybrid-mismatch classification regime applies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA), governed principally by French law and the EU VAT Directive.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for a foreign taxable person making transactions for which French VAT registration is required; France generally does not provide a registration threshold for such non-established businesses. The domestic small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base) has separate turnover limits, generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and EUR 37,500 for services, subject to applicable statutory rules, prior-year tests, and EU small-enterprise scheme rules. These exemption limits are not a general threshold for foreign businesses or for transactions outside the exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not generally require real-time tax-authority clearance or digital stamping of each VAT invoice. For domestic B2B transactions within scope, mandatory electronic invoicing is being phased in: all businesses must be able to receive e-invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance begins on that date for large and intermediate-sized businesses and is scheduled from 1 September 2027 for SMEs and micro-enterprises. In-scope invoices must use a compliant structured format and be transmitted through an approved platform (plateforme agréée, formerly PDP) or the public portal as permitted by the applicable rules. Electronic transaction and payment data reporting (e-reporting) applies to specified transactions outside the e-invoicing mandate, including relevant B2C and cross-border transactions. Applicable rollout dates and technical requirements should be verified against current legislation and DGFiP guidance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the EU may be exempt with a right to deduct input VAT, subject to the statutory conditions and evidence that the goods actually left the EU. The supplier must retain the export customs declaration and reliable evidence of exit. Intra-Community supplies may qualify for exemption with a right to deduct where the buyer is identified for VAT in another Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, and the supplier satisfies applicable invoicing, reporting, and evidence requirements. Services are not zero-rated merely because the customer is offshore: their VAT treatment depends on place-of-supply rules, customer status, service category, and any applicable exemption. For a B2B service supplied to a taxable customer established outside France, the general place-of-supply rule commonly places taxation where the customer is established, subject to exceptions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration showing the export procedure and the relevant MRN
Customs confirmation of exit from the EU or other reliable evidence of actual export
Commercial invoice identifying the parties, goods, values, and applicable VAT treatment
Transport evidence appropriate to the route, such as a bill of lading, sea waybill, CMR, or air waybill
Purchase order, contract, delivery records, and proof of payment where relevant to substantiate the transaction
Inward remittance or bank records where available and relevant; French law does not impose a universal inward-remittance certificate requirement for VAT zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No general French statutory deadline requires export proceeds to be repatriated to France; EU capital-movement rules generally permit cross-border transfers, subject to reporting, sanctions, and other applicable controls. If export or exemption conditions are not substantiated, the DGFiP may assess output VAT, deny or recover input-VAT deductions or refunds, and charge late-payment interest, generally 0.20% per month under the applicable rules. Tax penalties may include a 40% surcharge for deliberate failure and an 80% surcharge in specified cases of fraudulent conduct or abuse, subject to statutory qualifications and procedural rights. Serious conduct may also entail criminal exposure.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank) with the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) and the General Directorate of the Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery administering monetary, banking and external financial regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a eurozone and EU member, applies full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the French Monetary and Financial Code. There are no systemic exchange controls, no mandatory conversion for trade proceeds and no investment authorisation gates for ordinary inbound equity or shareholders loans. Regulatory formalities are limited to balance-of-payments declarations to the Banque de France for significant flows, EU/UN sanctions compliance, and standard fiscal/dividend procedures. Profit remittance via dividends, interest, royalties or intercompany repayment is lawful and not subject to FX authorisation, provided the underlying transactions are economically substantiated and timely reported at the applicable threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender regime exists in France. Exporters are free to retain, use, and convert export receipts without any mandatory conversion ratio, statutory timeline, or designated bank account requirement. However, the Banque de France requires balance-of-payments reporting for cross-border transactions above the prevailing declaration threshold (currently €750,000 per payment for non-bank filers through intermediary banks), and proceeds arising from qualifying export contracts must be traceable within the enterprise accounting records.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Banking
Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate and conditional. A non-EEA electronic money institution cannot operate in France without either an ACPR licence or an EU/EEA home-state authorization passporting through the Single Euro Payments Area. Off-balance-sheet digital EMIs lack the full prudential standing and documentary infrastructure for maritime instalment LCs and escrow accounts, and many are unwilling to support the medium-risk enhanced due diligence profile required for a large vessel shipyard. They are viable for onboarding an ancillary collection account or for facilitating initial low-value deposits, but the primary banking relationship should rest with a tier-1 French credit institution to support capital escrow and commercial LC workflows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/CFT law under the Monetary and Financial Code does not impose a blanket statutory requirement for a physical board meeting for every opening. Remote identification using secure video verification or certificate-based electronic signatures may be legally recognised under certain conditions, but in practice tier-1 banks require the signing director or the ultimate beneficial owner to appear at an initial in-person interview or to present notarially certified passport pages and apostilled corporate resolutions. For a non-resident-owned SAS in an enhanced-scrutiny industry, at least one director must normally physically attend the bank's financial centre or a foreign branch of the bank; the chosen signatories must also have verified and certified identities and be registered on the mandate resolutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and substantial shareholder funds entering France from a non-EU jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Kbis extract, in-force articles of association, registry of beneficial owners (RBE) filing, complete ownership diagram with apostilled corporate documents, passport/identity copies with notarial certification listed before a notary, bank reference letters from the originating banks, source-of-funds pack (selling contracts, audited statements or current-account attestations), and written confirmation that there are no politically exposed persons linked to the capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Vessel construction contract with staged contracting payments, multiple intermediaries and export sales to non-OECD buyers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully negotiated commercial shipbuilding contract and the corresponding financing facility, treasury payment schedule, vessel export licence confirmation or declaration, EU/UN sanctions screening records for every counterparty and beneficial owner, and evidenced documentary collection or LC referral letter issued by the lead arranging bank and the export credit agency where applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore or opaque holding structure involving trusts, foundations or entities in jurisdictions with low tax transparency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explicit UBO declaration identifying every natural person owning more than 25% of the economic rights or shares, legal opinions demonstrating economic substance, trust deed or foundation constitutional document provided under confidentially obligations modelled on the bank's compliance requirements, tax residency certificates and years of audited financial statements in French or English for each entity in the perimeter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unanticipated operational payments for vessel outfitting or supplier advances that exceed a bank's mitigated exposure threshold
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved internal remittance policy adopted by the SAS board, details of each underlying commercial invoice and delivery certificate, third-party quote validations, assignment or pledge oan confidentiality te, and a sworn statement that the payment is not being applied to sanctioned goods, dual-use items or embargoed re-export.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity, shareholders loans and advances must arrive in EUR generally, under SWIFT MT103, from the shareholder's licensed bank and bear the precise Banque de France balance-of-payments nature code for direct investment on the transaction certificate (or be declared by the receiving bank). The wire should include the SAS's SIREN and SIRET identifiers, the corporate LEI, and a clear settlement reference in the remittance information such as 'Equity contribution, SAS FR_SAS, capital reservation number'. For amounts exceeding the Banque de France threshold, submit the statistical return through the receiving bank or directly in the dedicated BDP-BAM portal listing the sender, the beneficial owner and the amount. For the Capital Escrow Account, the funding evidence package, including board resolution, source-of-funds statements and the notarising of the wiring will remain in the bank's compliance archive.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments are executed through (1) customary SWIFT MT103 payments for open-account invoices against commercial documentation; (2) irrevocable commercial letters of credit (Documentary Credits) for the strongest control when subject to the International Standby Practices ISP98 or UCP 600; (3) MT202 COV for clearing central treasury settlement between the SAS and its nominated negotiation bank; and (4) escrow releases against certification milestones. High-value instalments for hull modules, engine units or outfitting equipment should be routed through the LC issuing bank to the seller's corresponding bank with full beneficiary name, invoice date, BL/airway bill reference and delivery certificate to prevent sanctioned rejects and dual-use misuse.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD and major trade currencies)
FX options (OTC European-style, bought and sold under ISDA master agreements)
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) where the shipbuilding financing invoice contains a non-EUR benchmark
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted when the underlying exposure settlement is permitted in the non-convertible reference currency so declared

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: General Meeting Approval of Annual Accounts (AGO — Assemblée Générale Ordinaire)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' decision recorded in the corporate minute book; audited accounts subsequently transmitted to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal-year close (Art. L232-23 C. com.); for a December 31 FYE, approval no later than June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: President exposed to a €500 mandatory fine; failure to convene does not suspend tax-filing obligations; shareholders may petition the court to appoint a representative to call the meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts, Management Reports and Statutory Auditors' Report (Dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (commercial court registry) via Guichet unique / Infogreffe electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of shareholder approval; hard cut-off at 7 months from fiscal year-end (Art. R232-13 C. com.)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Mandatory €500 fine per late filing; continued default for two fiscal years exposes the company to judicial strike-off (radiation) at the Public Prosecutor's request and blocks corporate tax loss carry-forward set-offs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Declaration — Annual Status Confirmation and Update (DDOE — Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (filed together with the annual accounts deposit via Guichet unique)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Re-filing within 30 days after any share-transfer-induced change of a >25% beneficial owner or controlling interest; annual confirmation filed simultaneously with the annual accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Willful omission: up to 6 months' imprisonment and €7,500 fine; refusal to provide information to Registry or tax authorities: €1,000 for individuals and €5,000 for companies per request.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Liasse fiscale n° 2065 series) including IS declaration and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP — Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (mandatory e-filing on impots.gouv.fr/pro)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For December 31 FYE: e-filing by May 3 of the following year; for non-calendar fiscal years: within 3 months and 15 days after FYE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers 10% penalty on assessed tax, increased to 40% after formal notice and 80% in fraud cases, plus 0.20% monthly delay interest; tax losses are not set-off-able until the return is filed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Economic Contribution — Property-Based Business Tax (CFE — Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises) annual return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP — SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment and annual declaration due December 15 of the assessment year; new shipyard operations must file a start-up declaration within 3 months of commencement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% late-payment penalty plus delay interest; omissions or under-declarations subject to DGFIP reassessment within the standard limitation period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Business Tax (CVAE) declaration n° 1330 and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFIP — SIE (declaration filed through the 2069-SD system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Abolished for fiscal years 2024 onward under Article 55 of the 2024 Finance Act; residual 2023-year declarations remained due in 2024 and no recurring 2025 filing applies for 2024 revenues
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-applicable for FY 2024 onward; adjustments for earlier fiscal years remain assessable within the standard 3-year statute of limitation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SAS must appoint a French statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) when exceeding, at the end of a fiscal year, two of the three following thresholds: total balance sheet > €4.0M; net turnover exclusive of VAT > €8.0M; average permanent workforce > 50 employees. Appointment must occur within one year of the thresholds being surpassed. A commercial shipyard of this scope typically exceeds the turnover and balance-sheet criteria and must therefore engage an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (PCG — Plan Comptable Général, ANC Regulation No. 2014-03 and subsequent updates); consolidated accounts, if the shipyard forms a group, follow IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation is performed electronically with the annual accounts deposit: the company certifies that the registered beneficial owners remain current. Any share transfer causing an individual to hold directly or indirectly more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or to acquire control, must be re-declared to the Registry within 30 days of the transfer being registered in the securities register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders' decisions and minutes (dossier des décisions des associés — SAS)
Securities register and share-transfer registration (registre des valeurs mobilières)
Statutory corporate documents file (reports, audited accounts, shipbuilding licenses; kept at the registered office)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 – 900 per year (premium domiciliation with port-authority compliance support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – 22,000 per fiscal year (independent audit under French GAAP pursuant to Art. L823-12 C. com.)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced CIT 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for eligible small enterprises; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CIIC) at 20% for new product prototypes; Patent Box regime at 10% on qualified IP income. As a conservative deferred-tax assumption for this shipyard dossier, a 5-year loss-recognition horizon is applied; statutorily, French loss carry-forward is unlimited but annual utilization is capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of the excess taxable profit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultats n°2065-EN / 2065-SD (liasse fiscale including the 2031 and 2050-series annexes); filed through the secure EFI-Méga electronic system on impots.gouv.fr, with EDI transmission for consolidated groups and professional tax advisers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual declaration with four quarterly advance corporate income tax instalments and a final settlement at the filing deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, e-filing is due no later than the second working day after 1 May of the following year; for other year-ends, the statutory deadline is within three months of the balance-sheet date, extended by one month for electronic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, ISIC 3011 / NAICS 336611 activity code, fiscal closing date, and the identity and address of every non-resident direct or ultimate shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must be disclosed in the beneficial-ownership declaration; no anonymity or bearer-share arrangement is permitted; the SAS must also update the French UBO register simultaneously.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre A / Bénéfice ou déficit comptable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before corporate income tax, computed under French GAAP; includes shipyard construction revenue, long-term contract progress billing, escrow interest income, and exchange gains or losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income attributable to the French SAS is taxable in France; expenses charged by the non-resident parent must be limited to arm's-length, transfer-priced services with supporting time records and substantiation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre B / Résultat fiscal après rectifications extra-comptables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result adjusted for tax law: add-back of non-deductible expenses, elimination of exempt income, depreciation recapture, and application of special shipbuilding incentive provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholding group cannot book head-office cost allocations, group royalty charges, or shareholder management fees unless the French shipyard receives a real and proportionate benefit evidenced by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre H / Imputation des déficits antérieurs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year French tax losses used against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses genuinely incurred by the French SAS are available; a loss transferred into France from a foreign merger is ring-fenced. Annual loss utilization is limited to EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit above that ceiling.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cadre I / Crédits d'impôts et imputations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits such as the Research Tax Credit (CIR), Innovation Tax Credit (CIIC), and foreign withholding tax credits on income already taxed offshore.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French entity may claim CIR and CIIC credits regardless of foreign ownership; however, non-resident shareholders cannot offset the French dividend withholding tax against the SAS's corporate income tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty accrues at 5% per month, capped at 50% of the tax due; failure to file within 30 days of a formal notice triggers an automatic 10% penalty. Late payment interest runs at 0.20% per month. Willful misinterpretation carries a 40% civil penalty; organized fraud carries an 80% penalty under Art. 1729 CGI; officers can also face daily astreinte fines for failure to produce documents.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for corporate non-resident shareholders (Art. 119 bis 2 CGI); 30% for non-resident individuals, comprising 12.8% income tax plus 17.2% social levies; 0% may apply under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of the SAS for at least two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident shareholder or lender must deliver to the SAS a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the relevant tax authority, accompanied by a beneficial-ownership declaration and, for treaties with limitation-of-benefits clauses, an additional substance statement. The documents must be received before the cash distribution or interest payment. Where reduced withholding cannot be implemented at source, the non-resident may apply for a refund to the French tax office (SIE du siège) using form 5000/5001 or the ordinary réclamation procedure within the statutory six-year limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties for the use of patents, ship designs, or manufacturing processes paid to non-residents attract domestic withholding of 33.33%, reduced under most tax treaties to 0%–10%. Interest on arm's-length commercial debt is not subject to French withholding tax under domestic law; however, interest paid to controlling corporate shareholders can be recharacterized as deemed dividends at 25% when thin-capitalization limits or tax shelter rules are exceeded.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 in French group consolidated annual revenue or total consolidated assets triggers mandatory Master File and Local File preparation and filing under Articles L.13 AA and L.13 AB CGI; below this threshold, the SAS must retain a proportionate arm's-length documentation file for audit defense.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France applies no offshore ESR regime; instead, the General Anti-Abuse Rule (Art. L64 LPF), EU ATAD/DAC6, CFC legislation, and OECD BEPS principles require real economic presence. A functioning shipyard with physical yards, employed engineers and tradesmen, procurement authority, vessel design activity, classification-society oversight, and French regulatory licenses constitutes strong economic substance and should be preserved in all governance and intercompany contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating the shipyard's French taxable profit by omitting escrow-release milestones, inflating component purchase prices from a group supplier, or failing to disclose liquidated-damages indemnities received from a shipowner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 40% for bad faith and 80% for organized fraud under Art. 1729 CGI; default interest of 0.20% per month; criminal fine under Art. 1741 of up to EUR 500,000 or six times the evaded tax plus five years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable under Art. L.267 LPF for the corporate tax debt where they intentionally conceal assets; personal bank accounts and real estate are seizable, and courts may impose a travel ban, a five-year management disqualification, and imprisonment for a tax-evasion conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the French SAS as an invoice-staging shell with no local workforce, no production yard, no board decisions in France, and routing all shipbuilding margin to a zero-tax related entity through circular invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the entire scheme under the GAAR with full tax reversal; 80% penalty where the arrangement has no purpose other than tax avoidance; cancellation of refundable tax credits; possible dissolution of the company for sham management.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Judges can pierce the corporate veil, rendering directors personally liable for taxes, interest and penalties; executives face civil restitution, freezing orders, travel bans, and a professional ban preventing them from managing any French company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Executing a maritime installment letter of credit or escrow release for a vessel sale knowing that the buyer or beneficial owner is subject to UN/EU/OFAC sanctions, or where the escrow proceeds are derived from corruption or arms-related illicit dealing, without filing a suspicious-transaction report with TRACFIN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 1 million or four times the sums laundered; asset freezing orders; withdrawal of the shipyard's export or maritime license; criminal penalties under the Customs Code of up to five years' imprisonment and unlimited asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face individual criminal liability, personal asset seizure, travel bans, and prohibition from international trade; the compliance officer and signatories are equally exposed where they fail to block sanctioned payments or file the required suspicious transaction report.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging intercompany hull components at manipulated prices that force an artificially low margin for the French shipyard, or funding the vessel construction through excessive shareholder debt while deducting inflated interest, without meeting the arm's-length standard.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax recharacterization of the controlled transaction; adjustment of taxable income; 40% penalty under Art. 57 CGI, increased to 80% if the profit is transferred to a privileged tax jurisdiction; where required documentation is not produced within 30 days, a penalty equal to 5% of the undocumented transaction value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign knowingly false intercompany agreements or issue fictitious pricing certificates risk personal civil liability for the resulting tax shortfall; in aggravated cases, the French criminal court can issue travel bans, impose custodial sentences, and order restitution from personal estates.
